target_customer: Front-end developers and designers who want to host static websites without managing servers
problem: Designers and front-end developers needed a simple way to host and ship websites without setting up servers or back ends.
business_model: Subscription hosting plans (Prototype $2.99 per month, Personal $12.99 per month at the December 2013 launch)
product_category: Static website hosting and CMS synced with Dropbox

founders.name: Cole Krumbholz
previous_startups: Backlift (acquired by Squarespace per CB Insights)
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder in the TechCrunch launch article of 2013-12-05. The YC page lists no founder names. Other co-founders were not found.

exit.reason: Squarespace bought the Brace team and disabled Brace sites after 2015-01-19; terms undisclosed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Syncing Dropbox folders to a draft and production pipeline on AWS with a CDN and a ship button is moderate engineering for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Static hosting driven by a Dropbox folder was easy to copy and the plans were priced at a few dollars a month, with no data or network effects.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Squarespace acquired the Brace team in November 2014, shutting the product after January 19, 2015.

market_need_then: No dated demand evidence beyond the product launch. The YC listing describes Brace as the new way to host a site, simple as saving files in Dropbox.

branding.domain_note: Used the .io domain brace.io. It now redirects to a GoDaddy for sale page.
branding.community_and_virality: Gizmodo and Hacker News commenters noted the product's similarity to Backlift, but no merch or fan community was found.

brand_strength.rationale: TechCrunch, Gizmodo and Next Web covered the launch and acquisition, but the name is generic and shared with several unrelated companies, with no distinct identity found.

pivots.from: Backlift, a back-end service for front-end developers synced with Dropbox
pivots.to: Brace, Dropbox powered static site hosting
pivots.why: Not stated. Sources show the same founder built both and that Brace reused Backlift elements; the YC W12 listing text still describes Backlift.

outcome_analysis: Brace entered YC Winter 2012, likely as the Backlift back-end service for front-end developers, and relaunched in December 2013 as Dropbox powered static site hosting with low priced plans. Squarespace announced in November 2014 that it was acquiring the Brace team, paying customers got a year of Squarespace, and Brace sites were disabled after January 19, 2015. No funding or deal terms were found, so the outcome reads as a small team acquihire rather than a growth story.
notes: The YC page and an altss listing suggest the W12 company was Backlift, renamed Brace; the link rests on Gizmodo, CB Insights and the altss description, not on an opened company statement. CB Insights lists Squarespace and Y Combinator as Backlift investors, with no amounts, so no round is recorded. Funding searches returned only an unrelated mortgage company named Brace, which is excluded. The Squarespace press page said it acquired the team in January 2015 while Next Web dates the announcement to 2014-11-17. No dated competitors were found for 2012; the Backlift search returned only TechCrunch launch coverage without named rivals, so the list is empty. Exit type acquisition conflicts with the YC Inactive status only in label; YC does not distinguish acquired companies here.
